title: Endpoint IDM, Endpoint EDM and Share Files Externally

prose.text: Whether any of these has an API, SDK or Terraform surface is open {{gap:api-surface}}. The rules that use the resulting engines are in [[zia.dlp.endpoint-rules]], and the dictionary types are in [[zia.dlp.dictionaries]].

endpoint-idm-independent.statement: Endpoint IDM fingerprints are distributed to all Data Loss Prevention (DLP) endpoints. The Endpoint IDM operates in parallel to the Inline DLP IDM, enforcement and detection are independent, and reindexing of IDM files using the Endpoint DLP is required. The feature is in limited availability; access is through the Zscaler Account team.

quotes: These fingerprints are then distributed to all Data Loss Prevention (DLP) endpoints.
The Endpoint IDM operates in parallel to the Inline DLP IDM. Enforcement and detection are independent and require reindexing of IDM files using the Endpoint DLP.
This feature is in limited availability. To access this feature, contact your Zscaler Account team.
The Endpoint IDM operates in parallel to the Inline DLP IDM. Enforcement and detection are independent and require reindexing of IDM files using the Endpoint DLP.

fingerprint-size-limit.statement: Total Size of Fingerprints indicates the total size of all distributed indexed document fingerprints, and the admin can set the limit up to 100 MB.

quotes: Total Size of Fingerprints: Indicates the total size of all distributed indexed document fingerprints. The admin can set the limit up to 100 MB.
The admin can set the limit up to 100 MB.

idm-match-accuracy.statement: The settings article lists the match tests per accuracy level. Low: a user-uploaded document matches at least 25% of an indexed document, or an indexed document matches at least 50% of the user-uploaded document. Medium: the same two tests at 50% and 75%. High: a user-uploaded document matches at least 75% of an indexed document. The endpoint determines match accuracy in priority order High, Medium, then Low, and halts once a valid match is confirmed. Exclude 100% Match stops the dictionary triggering for documents that are a 100% match of already indexed documents.

quotes: A user-uploaded document matches at least 25% of an indexed document.
An indexed document matches at least 50% of a user-uploaded document.
A user-uploaded document matches at least 50% of an indexed document.
An indexed document matches at least 75% of a user-uploaded document.
High Accuracy: Zscaler detects a high-accuracy match when a user-uploaded document matches at least 75% of an indexed document.
When processing a file, the endpoint determines its match accuracy based on priority, starting with High, then Medium, and then Low. The process halts once a valid match is confirmed.
Select Exclude 100% Match if you do not want Zscaler to trigger the dictionary for documents that are a 100% match of already indexed documents.
When processing a file, the endpoint determines its match accuracy based on priority, starting with High, then Medium, and then Low. The process halts once a valid match is confirmed.

idm-process-and-limits.statement: Users can select up to 20 files per operation, with a maximum of 100 MB per file and a total maximum file size per session of 1 GB. Authorized users right-click sensitive files on their endpoint and select Index Documents, which creates and uploads file fingerprints to the cloud; the admin activates the policy, distributing the updated IDM package to all endpoints, and configures Endpoint DLP rules using the IDM-linked DLP engines.

quotes: Users can select up to 20 files per operation. The maximum size is 100 MB per file, and the total maximum file size per session cannot exceed 1 GB.
Authorized users can right-click sensitive files on their endpoint and select the Index Documents option. This creates and uploads file fingerprints to the cloud.
The admin activates the policy, distributing the updated IDM package to all endpoints.
Admins configure Endpoint DLP rules using the IDM-linked DLP engines to enforce policies.
Users can select up to 20 files per operation. The maximum size is 100 MB per file, and the total maximum file size per session cannot exceed 1 GB.

edm-hybrid.statement: Unlike methods such as IDM or OCR that are processed entirely on the device, full EDM inspection uses a local prefiltering mechanism that identifies candidate files on the endpoint, and only the flagged candidate files are transmitted to the cloud for comprehensive evaluation. After the cloud confirms a match, the classification result is stored locally on the endpoint, which uses it to enforce DLP policies across removable storage, network shares, personal cloud storage, application file access and printing, including when the device is offline.

quotes: Unlike methods such as IDM or OCR that are processed entirely on the device, full EDM inspection requires the following approach:
A local prefiltering mechanism identifies candidate files on the endpoint.
Only the flagged candidate files are transmitted to the cloud for comprehensive evaluation.
After the cloud confirms a match, the classification result is stored locally on the endpoint.

The endpoint uses the stored classification to enforce DLP policies across supported channels (i.e., removable storage, network shares, personal cloud storage, application file access and printing). Enforcement works even when the device is offline.

edm-setup.statement: The Understanding Exact Data Matching page says Endpoint EDM follows the same process as inline web DLP, as the rule evaluation for endpoint EDM occurs in the cloud: define a dictionary with the EDM type, add it to a DLP engine, and select it within Endpoint DLP rules. Continuous Classification and EDM Settings must be enabled in the Configurations tab. The EDM Optimizer must use the exact same CSV file that was uploaded to the Index Tool, with at least three columns designated as a Dictionary or a Regular Expression, and the tool validates that the selected column types match at least 90% of the CSV data. After the EDM is activated, the prefilter criteria are automatically pushed to all managed endpoints.

quotes: Follow the same process as inline web DLP, as the rule evaluation for endpoint EDM occurs in the cloud. Define a dictionary with the EDM type, add it to a DLP engine, and select it within your Endpoint DLP rules.
You must use the exact same CSV file that was uploaded to the Index Tool.
Select at least three columns to serve as the prefiltering criteria. Designate each column as either a Dictionary (for named entities) or a Regular Expression (for pattern-based data like IDs).
The tool validates that the selected column types match at least 90% of the CSV data to ensure accuracy.
After the EDM is activated, the EDM prefilter criteria are automatically pushed to all managed endpoints.
Ensure the Continuous Classification and EDM Settings are enabled in the Configurations tab.

edm-limitations.statement: EDM is not supported for Clipboard, and printing is only supported on Windows when using Microsoft Office or Adobe Reader.

quotes: EDM is not supported for Clipboard.
Printing is only supported on Windows when using Microsoft Office or Adobe Reader.

edm-page.statement: The EDM page shows the combined count of data entries across all active EDM prefilter files, and the users authorized to use the EDM Optimizer utility on their local systems. Each prefilter has a Status (for example Active, Inactive, or Pending), and the Edit icon disables the exact data match prefilter file.

quotes: Total Number of Records: The combined count of all data entries across all active EDM prefilter files.
Users Allowed to Run EDM Optimizer: The specific administrators or users authorized to use the EDM Optimizer utility on their local systems to generate prefilter criteria.
Status: The current operational state of the prefilter (e.g., Active, Inactive, or Pending).
Click the Edit icon to disable the exact data match prefilter file.

share-externally-settings.statement: Share Files Externally settings for external domains are None (prevent files being shared with any external domain), Specific Domains (restrict sharing to a predefined list of authorized domains) and Any Domain (allow sharing with all external domains without restriction). Specific Users grants external file sharing permission only to a defined list of users, groups, or departments. To enable changes, the change must be activated.

quotes: None: To prevent files from being shared with any external domains.
Specific Domains: To restrict file sharing to a predefined list of authorized domains.
Any Domain: To allow all files to be shared with all external domains without restriction.
Specific Users: To grant external file sharing permission only to a defined list of users, groups, or departments.
To enable the changes, you must activate the change.

share-externally-flow.statement: In the Secure File for External Sharing window the user can add up to 10 email recipients and click Protect File, and recipients must belong to the authorized domains configured in the Share Files Externally Settings page. The system encrypts the file locally and converts it into a secure HTML format, and the file is not transported by Zscaler during this step. The recipient must download the Zscaler Secure File Viewer tool for their operating system, and the system verifies the email's authorization and sends a One-Time Password (OTP) to the recipient's inbox. The feature encrypts files without automatically sharing them, so the protected files can be shared via email, removable storage or any other method.

quotes: In the Secure File for External Sharing window, the user can add up to 10 email recipients and clicks Protect File.
Recipients must belong to the authorized domains configured in the Share Files Externally Settings page.
The system encrypts the file locally and converts it into a secure HTML format; the file is not transported by Zscaler during this step.
To view the content, the recipient must download the Zscaler Secure File Viewer tool for their specific operating system.
The system verifies the email’s authorization and sends a One-Time Password (OTP) to the recipient’s inbox.
This feature encrypts files without automatically sharing them with external recipients, allowing you to share the protected files via email or removable storage or any other method.

share-externally-admin-control.statement: Admins can monitor all decryption attempts and successful access events, and revoke access to any file at any time by deleting it from the list or editing the authorized recipient list. The list shows Shared With (the external email recipients authorized to decrypt and view the file) and a History of Shared Date, Recipient, and Action.

quotes: Monitor all decryption attempts and successful access events.
Revoke access to any file at any time by deleting it from the list or editing the authorized recipient list.
Shared With: The list of external email recipients authorized to decrypt and view the file.
History: View historical information about the file shared externally (i.e. Shared Date, Recipient, and Action).

api-surface.title: Whether Endpoint IDM templates, the EDM prefilter and Share Files Externally have an API, SDK or Terraform surface
api-surface.detail: These findings come from help articles only. zia.dlp.endpoint-dlp names no API, SDK or Terraform surface for them, and the SDK, Terraform and Automate sources were not checked for these features.
